key_insight: Medical imaging AI hallucinations are a cross-modality safety problem that needs unified taxonomy, detection, and lifecycle-based mitigation.
clinical_relevance: Hallucinated findings, laterality errors, and invented measurements can directly affect biopsy, staging, and treatment planning, so expert oversight remains essential.
method: Synthesized peer-reviewed studies, benchmark datasets, and FDA guidance
Compared hallucination patterns across five imaging modalities
Mapped mitigation strategies to FDA Total Product Lifecycle and Predetermined Change Control Plan frameworks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that three taxonomic frameworks together cover the imaging pipeline, and that general-purpose foundation models can outperform medical-specialized models on hallucination-specific benchmarks.
watch_item: Several mitigation methods may help only when combined, and AI-generated flags still often require expert correction before clinical use.
paper_title: Hallucination in Medical Imaging AI: A Cross-Modality Analytical Framework for Taxonomy, Detection, and Mitigation under Regulatory Constraints
